lens: SOUND (promo): narrator delivery and pacing, music fit, mix loudness and ducking, the ending
method: No audio playback was possible. I measured EBU R128 momentary and short-term loudness (0.1-0.5 s steps) on mix/master.wav, score/renders/m01.wav and narration/narration.wav, and checked them against absolute word times from narration/timeline.json (82.708 s clock). I read mix/loudness.json, qa/reports/latest.json, render/render-report.json, score/cues.json notes, score/analysis/m01.json and m01.png, the narration and voice stage summaries in film.json, and the contact sheets for ch04-s02, ch06-s01 and ch06-s02. I checked round 1's sound issues and the round-1 verdict fixes for m01, L0402, L0505, L0601, ch06-s02 and the global clock. LEDGER: film.json has no stages.fixes key at all (no round1-global or round1-shots), so no id is marked fixed, partial or skipped. I verified each routed fix against the measurements and sheets instead.

summary: Round 2 fixed most of what round 1 asked of the sound. The payoff triad L0601 now clears the music by 11.8 dB at a measured 171 wpm. The haze sits at full level from the first frame. The time chapter keeps a half-time thread, and the verdict now works as the hinge: an open Asus2 on 'starting over' and the D landing on the ch06 cut, a 12 dB lift. The four-beat hole is intact, and the narration's 0.7 s pre-gap makes the master drop to room tone (-57 LUFS M at 46.6-46.8 s) before 'No click', the purest silence in the film. The mix is clean: -16.0 LUFS I, -1.9 dBTP, LRA 2.7, no limiting and a calibrated 4.2 dB duck. Three things keep the sound from excellent. (1) The ending deflates. The tagline rides a bed that drains 10 dB under it, and the 'button' is a 3 dB bump. The last 2 s of the end card sit at -40 to -50 LUFS M, close to room tone, over a static card, and the button misses the caret settle by 0.34 s. A bright promo needs a sonic-logo button here, not air. (2) L0402 regressed to 8.5 dB of speech over music, the worst in the film. Its three plucked accents land on the onsets of 'staging', 'preview' and 'localhost'. (3) Chapters 2-4 are still breathless: 'Point it at your app' runs at 330 wpm, five lines run at 195-199, and some sentence gaps are 0.25 s, while 7.3 s of the 90 s target goes unused. Separately: the shelf UI shows no critic score because the film was last published at 21:11, before round 1's verdict (21:18). public/generated/replay-qa-promo has no review.json, and library.json still lists the 84.25 s cut (QA publish.current warns).

issues.problem: The shelf shows no critic score and an outdated film. generator/film/publish.mjs writes public/generated/<slug>/review.json from the newest qa/reviews/round-<n>/verdict.json, but the last publish ran at 21:11:16Z, seven minutes before round 1's verdict.json (21:18:35Z). The round-2 assemble did not publish, so public/generated/replay-qa-promo has no review.json, and library.json still says runtime 84.25 with ch05 at 37.04 s, against the current 82.71 s film. QA flags this: 'publish current warn: shelf copy is stale'. Structurally, film-assemble publishes before film-review runs, so even when it does publish, the score on the shelf is one round behind until the end-of-loop publish.
issues.fix: After this round's verdict.json is written, run `node generator/film/publish.mjs --slug replay-qa-promo` (local only). In .claude/workflows/film-loop.js, call publish (or a review.json-only refresh) right after each film-review verdict, not only after assemble and at loop end, so the shelf always shows the latest critic round.

At 79.455, play M1's answer resolved, a two-note filtered-saw pluck A4 to D5 (dotted-8th delay, no bells) over sub D1, plus one dry 909 rim clack, about 7 dB louder than now (cue about -20 LUFS M at the hit). Under the tagline, keep a low Dmaj9 pad (lpf 800, about -24 M) instead of releasing from 77.5, and release it into the button. Let the button ring at least 2.5 s, then fade over 1.5 s, so the last second of the film sits no lower than about -35 LUFS M in the master. Re-check fadeAfterStrike and lineMasking on L0602 (keep at least 11 dB).

issues.problem: L0402 ('Against staging, a preview, even localhost') regressed from 9.9 to 8.5 dB of speech over music, now the lowest margin in the film. The DRIVE section's three rising plucked accents land on b-staging 26.53, b-preview 27.12 and b-local 27.77, which are exactly the onsets of 'staging', 'preview' and 'localhost', the /st/ and /pr/ consonants. This is the line whose 'Against' was misheard in round 1, and its listening sign-off is still pending.
issues.fix: Keep the accents on the pill fills but make them dark transients: lpf 1500, 3-4 dB softer, and no dotted-8th delay tail running into the next word. Under L0402-L0404 (25.84-35.44), give the drive the same treatment the lift got under L0601: closed hats eased 3 dB at hpf 8500, open hat at velocity 0.25 or lower with hpf 9000. Target at least 11 dB on L0402 and L0403 without lowering the section's level in the gaps (24.64-25.84, 28.33-29.26).

issues.problem: 'Point it at your app.' is the product's core action and gives the M1 hook its name, but it is spoken in 0.91 s (8.00-8.91; 'it' 0.07 s, 'at' 0.08 s), which is 331 wpm on QA's per-shot measure and about twice the film's average. The action is thrown away in a blur right where the promo makes its first promise.

best_moments: The hinge verdict: an open felt-piano Asus2 under the tail of 'starting over' (66.26 s), then the full D landing on the ch06 cut (67.08 s). The music rises from -28 to -16 LUFS M, turning the cut into a resolution.

The four-beat hole on 'Four dropped frames' is intact (cue silent from about 45.3 to 47.1 s). With the 0.7 s pre-gap before 'No click', the master drops to room tone (-57 LUFS M at 46.6-46.8 s), and the kick returns on 'click'.
L0601's triad now lands as three beats: 171 wpm with 0.25 s breaks, 11.8 dB clear of the music, and the lift's brightness held in the gaps and the bloom.

The tape-stop after 'what's slow' still falls cleanly into the B-minor half-time chapter, and a soft half-time thread now runs under 'Twenty-five of twenty-seven', so the time chapter never loses its pulse.
The mix is clean: -16.0 LUFS I, -1.9 dBTP, LRA 2.7, no master limiting, a calibrated 4.2 dB duck and line levels within about 1 dB.
